observations: Five or six thin white lines run nearly horizontally across the full width, sitting on top of all other marks and dividing the field into loose bands.
Broad vertical strokes in sky blue and teal form a loose backdrop behind clusters of rounded yellow and orange shapes concentrated in the left and upper-center areas.
Short, blunt dabs in deep purple, forest green, and dark red appear in the middle and lower-center, sitting against the warm yellows around them.
reading: Horizontal white lines cross the image like ruled marks, holding a field of vertical color beneath them. Yellow and orange masses push upward while blue strokes fall downward, and the two movements meet without resolving. Small dark dabs in purple and green interrupt the warmth at the center, giving the image a cooler, quieter weight below its bright upper half. The mood reads as suspended rather than settled.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #35 and nnxyz nnotb #37. Both share the vertical-stroke structure but differ sharply: #35 uses a saturated pink ground with outlined forms, and #37 replaces the blue field with dense black and earth tones on white.

connections.reason: Both works layer crossing vertical and horizontal strokes into a grid-like field, but #37 replaces the light blue ground and white overlay lines with black and red marks on white, producing a much heavier visual weight.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the white horizontal lines cross over the colored marks, and does that crossing change how you read the depth of the image at those points?
